solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Upper-class toff with refined virtues escaping attention?

parts.note: a nob is a toff, a posh person

indicators.note: refined suggests the letters of virtues are processed into a new form

explanation.surface: A posh toff whose genteel virtues let him slip by unnoticed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'refined' seems to praise the virtues, but it is the anagram signal, giving TRUSIVE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that escapes attention is inconspicuous, not drawing notice, which is the adjective's sense.

clue.text: Novelist gets fix about French city

indicators.note: about says the fix word goes around the city

parts.note: to nail something is to fix it in place
Pau is a city in south-west France

explanation.surface: A writer sorts something out around a city in France.
explanation.definitionFit: V. S. Naipaul was a Trinidad-born Nobel-winning novelist, author of A House for Mr Biswas.

clue.text: Magistrates note point of reference

parts.note: magistrates sitting in court are collectively the bench
to mark is to note or notice

explanation.surface: Magistrates make a note of a key point.
explanation.definitionFit: A benchmark is a standard against which other things are measured or compared.

clue.text: Scope in pastime recently taken up

indicators.note: taken up says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: The range of a hobby someone has just adopted.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'taken up' reads the letters upwards; 'in' marks the hidden stretch.
explanation.definitionFit: A remit is the area of activity assigned to someone, their scope or brief.

clue.text: Drunk attending whether you like it or not!

definitions.text: whether you like it or not!

parts.note: a sot is a drunkard
someone attending is present, here

explanation.surface: A drunk turns up uninvited, like it or not.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drunk' looks like an adjective but is the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A defiant retort said to end an argument, implying the speaker will have their way regardless.

clue.text: Name adopted by fruit producer of a pedigree

indicators.note: adopted by says the name goes inside the fruit producer

parts.note: a vine produces grapes
a tag is a name or label

explanation.surface: A grape grower takes on a name with fine lineage.
explanation.definitionFit: Vintage describes something of high quality and long-established, old and classic, of good stock.

clue.text: Excessive on reflection, a Merc flying is caught by it?

definitions.text: Excessive on reflection, a Merc flying is caught by it?

indicators.note: is caught by says the other pieces sit inside the it word

parts.note: it is slang for sex appeal, abbreviated SA

indicators.note: on reflection says the excessive word is read backwards

parts.note: deep can mean intense or extreme

indicators.note: flying suggests letters scattering, so a Merc is rearranged

explanation.surface: A Mercedes driven too fast, reflected on afterwards, gets snapped by a roadside device.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it' is old slang for sex appeal. 'on reflection' gives PEED and 'flying' gives CAMER, both held by 'is caught by'. Read whole, the clue describes the device itself.
explanation.definitionFit: A roadside camera photographs vehicles travelling too fast, catching a speeding car.

clue.text: It's behind a top German magazine

parts.note: Stern is a leading German weekly news magazine

explanation.surface: A noted German periodical takes the back seat.
explanation.definitionFit: Astern means at or towards the rear of a ship, so behind.

clue.text: Go by club losing source of real enthusiasm

parts.note: to go by something is to pass it

indicators.note: losing says a letter is dropped from the club word

parts.note: an iron is a golf club

indicators.note: the source of a word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: Walking past a club that has lost its genuine zeal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing' drops R ('source of real') from IRON, leaving ION.
explanation.definitionFit: Passion is strong enthusiasm or fervour for something, a near synonym.

clue.text: Greek character leads insignificant rebellion

parts.note: mu is a letter of the Greek alphabet
insignificant can mean tiny, very small

explanation.surface: A Greek figure heads a minor uprising.
explanation.definitionFit: A mutiny is a rebellion, especially by sailors or soldiers against their officers.

clue.text: Complicated craft I cite with English in official declaration

indicators.note: complicated suggests something tangled, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A convoluted craft quoted alongside English in a formal statement.
explanation.definitionFit: A certificate is an official document attesting or declaring a fact.

clue.text: Pupil's here to bear investigation? Nonsense

parts.note: the pupil is found in the eye
informally, an excuse that will wash is one that bears scrutiny

explanation.surface: A school pupil is here to face an inquiry, which is dismissed as rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pupil' is a schoolchild on the surface but the part of the eye here.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyewash is informal for nonsense or humbug, talk meant to deceive.

clue.text: Support perhaps Arab League finally — close to a majority?

parts.note: a golf tee is an example of a support for the ball
an Arab is a breed of horse, and a nag is a horse

indicators.note: finally picks the closing letter of the word League

explanation.surface: Backing the Arab League in its final stages, almost a majority vote.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arab League' looks like one political body, but Arab is a horse (NAG). The 'majority' is the age of adulthood, 18.
explanation.definitionFit: A teenager's years lead up to the legal age of adulthood, so they are near coming of age.

clue.text: Ditch by a lake and waterway

parts.note: to can something is informally to ditch or scrap it
L is the map abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: A trench beside a lake and a stream.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ditch' looks like a noun for a channel but is the verb to scrap.
explanation.definitionFit: A canal is an artificial channel for boats, a type of waterway.

clue.text: Feel bitter with following court professionals currently

indicators.note: with following places the bitter word after the tennis body

parts.note: the ATP is the Association of Tennis Professionals, players on the court
to resent something is to feel bitter about it

explanation.surface: Someone resentful of the tennis pros in the current season.
explanation.walkthrough: 'court' suggests law, but it is the tennis court.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean now, at this moment in time, an adverbial phrase and its synonym.

clue.text: A piece at college getting more colourful?

parts.note: per means a, as in five pounds a head
a king is a chess piece
up means in residence at university

explanation.surface: One coin per student, as they become livelier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'piece' suggests a coin or slice but is the chessman.
explanation.definitionFit: Perking up means brightening or becoming livelier, more colourful in spirit.

clue.text: Spooner's creator of rugby formations — whence comes dirt?

indicators.note: the Reverend Spooner swapped the opening sounds of words, so the two words' first letters trade places

parts.note: a ruck is a loose scrum in rugby
a maker creates

explanation.surface: Asking who designs rugby set pieces, and where the mud on the players comes from.
explanation.walkthrough: A muckraker is a journalist who digs up scandal, the dirt of the question.
explanation.definitionFit: A muck-raking journalist digs up scandal, so they are the source of the dirt.

clue.text: Islander in yard detained by copper upset over disorder

indicators.note: in a down clue over places the first part above the disorder
detained by says the yard letter is held inside
upset says the copper letters are turned over

parts.note: a police constable, PC, is a copper
a riot is public disorder

explanation.surface: An islander is held in a yard by an angry policeman over a disturbance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'copper' looks like Cu, but is the police officer.
explanation.definitionFit: A Cypriot is a native of Cyprus, a Mediterranean island.

clue.text: Trouble amid sign of age barrier

indicators.note: amid says the trouble word sits inside the sign of age

parts.note: rings in a tree trunk show its age
to ail is to trouble

explanation.surface: Trouble among the elderly at a fence.
explanation.definitionFit: A railing is a fence of rails, a barrier.

clue.text: Test requirement in court

definitions.meaning: a test, as in the ... of the pudding, or a trial print
evidence establishing a fact, demanded in a trial

explanation.surface: A trial needs evidence in court.
explanation.definitionFit: A test of strength is a proving, and a court requires evidence establishing guilt.

clue.text: Persist with unpredictability in service providers

indicators.note: with unpredictability says the letters fall in an unforeseen order

explanation.surface: Keep going despite erratic service from suppliers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'service' is a church service, not a utility.
explanation.definitionFit: Priests conduct church services, so they provide them.

clue.text: Choice drink after switch at start

indicators.note: switch at start says only the opening pair of letters change places

parts.note: a potion is a drink, often medicinal or magical

explanation.surface: Picking a drink after changing your mind at the outset.
explanation.definitionFit: An option is a choice, one of the alternatives available.

clue.text: What remains round parking area — or something similar

indicators.note: round says the remains word surrounds the parking letter

parts.note: a relic is something that survives from the past
P is the standard sign abbreviation for parking

explanation.surface: Ruins surrounding a car park, or a lookalike.
explanation.definitionFit: A replica is an exact copy, something closely similar to the original.

clue.text: Way of expressing interest about part of stage

parts.note: APR, annual percentage rate, expresses the interest on a loan
on means about, concerning

explanation.surface: An actor explains interest rates on a section of the stage.
explanation.definitionFit: The apron is the part of a theatre stage projecting in front of the curtain.

clue.text: Native expression with credit limited — senseless!

indicators.note: limited says each word is cut short, losing its final letter

parts.note: an idiom is an expression native to a language
tick is informal for credit, as in buying on tick

explanation.surface: A local saying about restricted borrowing is called stupid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'limited' trims both IDIOM and TICK, giving IDIO and TIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Something senseless is foolish or stupid, lacking good sense.

clue.text: Caribbean cyclist with day off is more flexible

parts.note: WI stands for West Indies, the Caribbean islands

indicators.note: off says the day letter is taken away

parts.note: a cyclist is a rider

explanation.surface: A West Indian cyclist on a rest day is suppler.
explanation.definitionFit: The comparative of wiry, lean and supple like bendable metal strands.

clue.text: My wine quietly drained — lack enough?

parts.note: my! and gosh! are both exclamations of surprise

indicators.note: drained says something is emptied out of the wine word

parts.note: port is a fortified wine
P is piano, the musical direction for quietly

explanation.surface: Someone notices their wine glass has been quietly emptied and wonders if they lack enough.
explanation.walkthrough: 'My' looks possessive but is the exclamation.
explanation.definitionFit: To go short is to do without, having too little of something needed.

clue.text: Spotting gas that's exploded in flying facility

indicators.note: something exploded has been blown apart, so these letters scatter into a new order

explanation.surface: Detecting a gas leak that blew up at an airfield.
explanation.definitionFit: A staging post is a regular stopping place on a route, such as an airfield where flights refuel.
